entries.license_or_terms: Public developer documentation on Boston Dynamics' developer site; no license grant for CAD is made there — the page points to the Support Center for CAD.
entries.notes: What it proves: payloads connect through a fully shielded, over-molded DB25 cable (keepout dimensions and sealing-gland geometry are published), and 'Detailed CAD is available on the Support Center' at the Defeatured Spot CAD Models article — the vendor's own pointer from public docs to the gated CAD.

entries.license_or_terms: Public developer documentation on Boston Dynamics' developer site.
entries.notes: The full DB25 payload-port pinout. Power pins 12, 13, 24, 25 (grounds 9, 10, 21, 22): supply range 35–59 V, absolute maximum 72 V, 3 A per pin, max 150 W per port, 150 µF per port bulk capacitance. Battery bus runs 35 V (discharged) to 58.8 V (full); the bus is clamped at 72 V and payload components 'should be selected to handle a maximum payload input voltage of at least 80 V'. Average power per payload connector must not exceed 150 W; a resettable limiter disables payload power when both ports combined exceed 9–13 A. Payload power needs the interlock loops closed (pins 5↔18, 6↔19, 8↔20, 11↔23). Ethernet 1000Base-T and a PPS signal are on the same connector. This page is the source for the re-based power story in the Jetson + LiDAR build.
entries.title: Payload Electrical Interface — Spot SDK documentation (5.2.0)

entries.license_or_terms: Public developer documentation on Boston Dynamics' developer site.
entries.notes: States the published payload limit used across this page: 'Spot can support 14 kg total combined capacity distributed over the top of the robot', and 'The Spot Arm weighs 8 kg. Total combined payload weight should be within the 14 kg maximum payload limit' — so the photographed unit's arm already draws 8 kg of the limit. Also: maximum recommended body-mounted payload width 190 mm, and a 3D STEP model of Spot's back 'is available upon request', with the body STEP (including typical leg-swing areas) on the Support Center. This page is also the one that links the official base URDF zip filed below.

The gate is stated publicly in the Support Center itself — the article 'Maintain and Customize Spot Leg and Body Panels' says 'Verified customers can log in to access defeatured Spot CAD models at Spot Downloads', and the Spot downloads/topics pages mark customer login as required. The article URL does not resolve for anonymous visitors (login-scoped), no login was attempted, and no CAD was downloaded.

entries.license_or_terms: Public Support Center article (readable without login).
entries.notes: Boston Dynamics' own expansion payload, mounted on the payload rails with M5 T-slot nuts: it turns one payload port into regulated power plus Ethernet. Regulated power output: a maximum of 150 W shared between the 12 V and 24 V outputs, and 5 V at a maximum of 10 W. The HD15 breakout pins are published: pins 1–4, 6 ground; 7, 8, 11, 12 = 12 V; 13–14 = 24 V; 15 = 5 V; pin 5 = PPS (5 V TTL). RJ45 provides 1000Base-T Ethernet. The unit weighs 430 g (the only added-part mass in the Jetson + LiDAR build that is published) and measures 50 × 192 × 67 mm. These figures re-base the build's power story.
entries.title: Spot General Expansion Payload (GXP) — Boston Dynamics Support Center

entries.license_or_terms: Boston Dynamics' published spec sheet (imprint bostondynamics.com, document updated 05/22/2024); this copy is hosted on a vendor CDN, which is recorded here rather than hidden.
entries.notes: The single most compact published statement of the payload interface — the Payload Mounting block: Max Weight = 14 kg (30.9 lbs); Mounting Area = 850 mm (L) × 240 mm (W) × 270 mm (H); Mounting Interface = M5 T-slot rails; Connector = DB25 (2 ports); Power Supply = Unregulated DC 35–58.8 V, 150 W per port. The 14 kg figure is independently stated in the SDK Configuration Requirements page filed above.

Its spot_description submodule — filed separately below — is the community URDF lineage. Nothing here is vendor CAD.

headline: Boston Dynamics does not publish an open CAD model of Spot. The detailed CAD is defeatured and sits in the Support Center behind a verified-customer login; the SDK documentation does publicly link one official base URDF (a zip whose contents and license were not inspected — see its entry). Everything else filed here is official interface documentation, or community models — labelled as such, never presented as the vendor's.
notes: Retrieval was text-only, operator-side, on 2026-10-28: pages were opened and read, no login was attempted anywhere, and no file was downloaded. Third-party corroboration of the CAD position: the robot-landscape models index (botlandscape.com/topics/models.html) records that 'Boston Dynamics points SDK users to defeatured detailed CAD in its Support Center rather than publishing meshes', and presents no third-party Spot mesh as a vendor model. A retrieval proposes; it never merges — figures from these sources enter a robot's curated spec only through a separate, reviewed curation step, the same propose-don't-auto-merge rule the Spotter grouping uses.
